name: GoMA
funding: Run by Glasgow Life for Glasgow City Council. Glasgow Life's supporters include Creative Scotland, the Scottish Government, Art Fund, the National Lottery Heritage Fund and Bloomberg Philanthropies.
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies is listed at Glasgow Life level, not for GoMA alone; the May 2026 letter targeted five London theatres.
records_note: Run by Glasgow Life, which posts annual reviews 2013-14 to 2025-26, charity accounts, a supporters list for 2025/26 and its board.

name: Compton Verney
funding: £5.07M income (FY to Mar 2026); Compton Verney Fund endowment, Arts Council NPO, members; local firms Silson, SE-Solicitors, Goldcrest.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Endowment derives from Peter Moores (Littlewoods pools), historic. Founded 1993 by the Peter Moores Foundation (Littlewoods pools and retail fortune); could be read as founding gambling money. Trust grants unread.
records_note: No annual reports; accounts 2023 to 2025 are on the Charity Commission register; corporate sponsors show as logos; trustees are listed with biographies.

name: Henry Moore Institute
funding: Part of the Henry Moore Foundation, funded from its investment portfolio. Leeds City Council gives £145,743 a year to the Institute; Arts Council England funds the Yorkshire Sculpture International partnership.
watch: The Foundation holds a restricted fund for Bloomberg Connects. 260 UK artists asked five London theatres to drop Bloomberg in May 2026; not targeted here.
records_note: Part of the Henry Moore Foundation, which posts reviews from 2010-11, trustees' reports and accounts 2015 to 2024, and its trustees; no funder list.

name: Bluecoat
funding: £2.4M income (FY2025); Arts Council, Liverpool City Council, Culture Liverpool.
watch: Trust list is from the FY2023 accounts (newest opened). Business members are not named publicly.
why_flagged: Trust list is from the FY2023 accounts (newest opened). Business members are not named publicly.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the homepage Funded by block is undated logos, and board members are listed.

name: FACT
funding: Arts Council England and Liverpool City Council are statutory funders. Paul Hamlyn, Jerwood, John Ellerman, Granada, Bloomberg Philanthropies and other trusts also give.
watch: More than 260 UK artists asked five London theatres to drop Bloomberg Philanthropies in May 2026; FACT was not named.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts sit on the Charity Commission register, funders show as undated logos, and the team page names the trustees.

name: Autograph
funding: Arts Council England and the National Lottery Heritage Fund (site footer). Projects backed by Art Fund, Paul Hamlyn Foundation and Cockayne Grants. Barclays gave to the 2007 building only.
watch: Rivington Place opened in 2007 with Arts Council lottery capital, Barclays, Hackney, the London Development Agency and the EU. No protest or censorship found.
records_note: One yearly impact summary (2025 to 2026), accounts on the Charity Commission register, funder logos only, and trustees listed on the team page.

name: Somerset House
funding: Trusts include AKO, Garfield Weston, Rothschild, Linbury and the National Lottery Heritage Fund. Corporate partners: Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, American Express, Virgin Atlantic Holidays, HSBC UK and Bloomberg.
watch: The ASA banned two HSBC climate adverts in October 2022. 260 UK artists asked London theatres to drop Bloomberg in May 2026; neither targeted here.
records_note: Annual reports with financial statements from 2014-15 to 2023-24 on its site, an undated named supporters page, and trustees listed.

name: HOME
funding: £7.2M income (FY2025); Arts Council England and Manchester City Council core funding.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Supporters page unreadable. Censorship row: Mar 2024 cancelled a Gaza writing event, reversed it after protest. Roster unread: homemcr.org blocks bots (412).
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the Our Supporters page names funders and patrons undated, and trustees are listed.

name: New Art Exchange
funding: £1.6M income (FY2025). Arts Council England £1.27M, about 79% of income; Power to Change (Freelands programme), Nottingham City Council, Nottingham Trent University, Art Fund.
watch: No flagged funder, protest or censorship found. Arts Council England is its main funder.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, funders show as one undated logo, and the board is listed.

name: Pier Arts Centre
funding: £618k income (FY2025). Creative Scotland and Orkney Islands Council; partner of Tate through the Plus Tate network.
watch: Collection founded by Margaret Gardiner's gift. No flagged funder or protest found.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the OSCR register, the Partnerships page names funders and partners undated, and the board is listed.

name: Cample Line
funding: £127k income (2025). Creative Scotland multi-year funding from April 2025, Holywood Trust, Henry Moore Foundation, Dumfries and Galloway Council, Regional Cultural Fund.
watch: Rural art space near Dumfries. Its website lists no funders; the signed 2025 accounts name them.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the OSCR register, funders show as unlabelled logos, and the Who We Are page lists the board.

name: Atlanta Contemporary
funding: $0.84M expenses (FY2023); Warhol and Ruth foundations, City of Atlanta, Fulton County, Arthur M. Blank family fund, Intuit, members.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Board page unavailable. In-kind sponsors include Post Meridiem Spirit Co (alcohol) and Orange Barrel Media (advertising). Leadership turnover 2025-26, no funder controversy.
records_note: No annual reports found; Form 990s for 2011 to 2023 are on ProPublica, a FY26 donors page names funders, and the board is listed.
